html:
A high-speed railway of about 1,300 km between Beijing and Shanghai, opened in June 2011. Trains run at up to 350 km/h, and the fastest take about four and a half hours.

It runs close to the line of the Grand Canal, the old trade artery between north and south, and passes Tianjin, Jinan and Nanjing. It soon became one of the busiest and most profitable high-speed lines in the world.

China opened its first high-speed line in 2008 and then built at great speed. By the 2020s it had more than 40,000 km of high-speed track, about two thirds of the world's total. The model was Japan's Shinkansen, and China bought early trains from Japanese and European makers before building its own. A century earlier, the Beijing to Zhangjiakou railway of 1909 had been the first line built by Chinese engineers. Taiwan opened its own high-speed rail in 2007.
